status: Admitted logical decoder implemented and tested; public/owned reader integration remains open
change: decodeBsonValue first validates framing, then constructs dynamic maps and arrays using an admitted explicit stack. Strings use fatal UTF-8 decoding; duplicate document keys reject rather than silently overwrite. Binary output is detached even for Node Buffer inputs. Array index strings are not materialized. Construction errors release partially built output; successful output ownership transfers to the parent scope.

valueContract.native: Documents use Map, arrays use Array, int32/double use number, int64 uses bigint, UTC datetime uses exact TimestampValue, and strings/booleans/null retain native values.
valueContract.tagged: BSON-specific values use maps carrying $bson plus explicit fields: binary (subtype, bytes), objectId (bytes), regex (pattern, options), dbPointer (namespace, id), code/symbol (value), codeWithScope (code, scope), timestamp (increment, seconds), decimal128 (bytes), undefined/minKey/maxKey.
valueContract.boundary: Decimal128 remains an explicitly tagged exact 16-byte value, not an implicitly rounded number or a claim of SQL decimal128 arithmetic. Regex and code are stored data, never evaluated. Tagged maps are a logical representation, not an automatic BSON re-encoding API; ordinary source documents may contain the same field names.

cases: Actual non-null BSON payloads extracted from the vendored Parquet fixture decode to expected dynamic maps

Minimum int64 integer and UTC milliseconds retain precision; negative zero retained

2000 nested output documents construct without recursive calls; framing separately tests 5000 levels
